# Results — Study 920 (Total Cost of Ownership) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py) — every table below is printed by
that script, cache-only and offline. Total cost of owning an index wrapper = **expense
ratio** + **realised tracking difference** + **round-trip spread**. Only the middle term is on
a daily-close tape; the fee is a prospectus number and the spread is a quote-level number, so
both are declared ASSUMPTIONS and swept. All returns are **daily total-return closes**
(`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`) — never price-only. Tracking difference is always quoted
**cheap minus liquid, in basis points per year**: positive means the cheaper wrapper really
did deliver more. One execution lag in the holding-period race (choice made through the close
of day *t*, both candidate positions entered at the close of day *t+1*). As-of **2026-06-30** —
partial calendar months and partial calendar years are dropped everywhere.*

## Two confounds and a selection, named before any number

- **The expensive leg is always a unit investment trust.** SPY (1993) and QQQ (1999) are
  UITs: by legal form they cannot reinvest dividends between distribution dates and cannot
  lend securities, so in a rising market they bleed a cash drag *on top of* their fee (Elton,
  Gruber, Comer & Li 2002). Every pair with a measured gap therefore mixes **fee gap + trust
  cash drag + lending pass-through**, and this study **cannot separate them** — there is no
  pair on the tape where a cheap open-end fund races an expensive open-end fund on the same
  index. Read every number here as *what the cheap wrapper delivered*, never as *what the fee
  cost*. The agreement with the prospectus gap (within ~2 bp) is the sum of at least two
  effects, not a confirmation of one.
- **The placebo controls the ruler, not the confound.** VOO vs IVV are both 3 bp open-end
  funds: the pair proves the estimator reads ≈ 0 when there is nothing to read, which is what
  a placebo is for. It has no UIT on either leg, so it cannot separate fee from trust form.
- **Survivorship.** These are the wrappers still trading at the as-of date. Cheap clones that
  closed never entered the sample, and a clone that closes is likelier to have tracked badly.
  The bias is small for a *fee* measurement — the fee gap is contractual, not
  performance-selected — but the sample is the survivors and it is not a random draw.

## The headline — the common window (2020-10-13 → 2026-06-30)

This is the only span on which every wrapper under test trades; it is fixed by **QQQM's
inception date**, not by any result. **All four pairs rest on the same five complete calendar
years — 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025** — so *n* = 5 everywhere, including the S&P pairs whose
own histories are far longer.

| Pair (cheap over liquid) | Stated fee gap | Realised TD | sd | *t* | Years + | Bootstrap CI | **Student-*t* CI** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **IVV over SPY** | +6.45 | **+5.78 bp/yr** | 4.43 | **+2.92** | 5/5 | [+3.55, +7.90] | **[+0.28, +11.28]** |
| **VOO over SPY** | +6.45 | **+6.60 bp/yr** | 4.34 | **+3.40** | 5/5 | [+3.46, +9.33] | **[+1.21, +11.99]** |
| VOO over IVV — **the placebo** | 0.00 | **+0.82 bp/yr** | 2.46 | +0.75 | 3/5 | [−0.25, +2.21] | **[−2.24, +3.88]** |
| **QQQM over QQQ** | +5.00 | **+7.19 bp/yr** | 3.05 | **+5.27** | 5/5 | [+4.78, +9.48] | **[+3.40, +10.98]** |

**Which interval to believe.** The block bootstrap resamples an empirical distribution of
*five* annual numbers and makes no allowance for the sd being estimated from those same five,
so it comes out far too narrow — IVV/SPY bootstraps to [+3.55, +7.90] where the Student-*t*
interval on the identical five numbers is [+0.28, +11.28]. **This document quotes the *t*
interval for every pessimistic claim.** All three fee-gap pairs still clear zero on it; IVV
over SPY only just.

The distribution-free statement is the cleanest one and owes nothing to either interval: each
of the three fee-gap pairs is **positive in all five years** (one-sided sign-test *p* = 1/32 =
0.031 each), while the same-fee placebo is positive in three of five. QQQM's five annual
tracking differences are **+2.2, +8.8, +10.1, +8.4, +6.5 bp** — every year of its life.

## The three estimators disagree — and the placebo says which one to believe

The same quantity, measured three ways on the same common window, is *not* the same number:

| Pair | **Annual (headline)** | Cumulative | Monthly ×12 | Opening stub | Complete years | Closing stub |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| IVV over SPY | **+5.78** | +3.38 | +3.90 | +5.7 bp | +28.9 bp | **−15.4 bp** |
| VOO over SPY | **+6.60** | +8.07 | +9.04 | +4.7 bp | +33.0 bp | +8.2 bp |
| VOO over IVV (**placebo**) | **+0.82** | **+4.69** | +5.14 | −1.0 bp | +4.1 bp | **+23.6 bp** |
| QQQM over QQQ | **+7.19** | +4.48 | +2.23 | −5.0 bp | +35.9 bp | −5.5 bp |

The last three columns decompose the window's total drift into the partial 2020 Q4 stub, the
five complete years, and the partial 2026 H1 stub. The annual estimator keeps only the middle
term; the cumulative estimator keeps all three. **The stubs are where the tape breaks.** Two
funds that both charge 3 bp cannot really drift **+23.6 bp apart in six months** — that is a
level artefact in a closing print, and it is four times the whole annual signal. It is what
lifts the placebo's *cumulative* estimate to +4.69 bp/yr, **above IVV-over-SPY's +3.38**.

So the headline is **estimator-conditional, and this is the study's sharpest caveat**: a
reader who prefers the raw cumulative drift gets no signal at all on the IVV/SPY pair. The
defence is not that the annual estimator is bigger; it is that the complete-calendar-period
rule was fixed ex ante by the as-of convention, and that the placebo pair — whose true gap is
zero by construction — demonstrates the contamination the rule removes. Two of the three
estimators (the annual one and the overlapping race further down) leave the placebo quiet; the
cumulative one does not.

## Why the full histories say less (and it is the tape's fault, not the funds')

| Pair | Window | Realised TD | *t* | Median | Trimmed mean (*t*) | Worst single year |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| IVV over SPY | 2000-05-19 → | +2.24 | +0.78 | +4.91 | +3.29 (+1.41) | 2016: **−40.9 bp** |
| VOO over SPY | 2010-09-09 → | +2.60 | +0.69 | +5.94 | +5.48 (**+4.65**) | 2014: **−47.3 bp** |
| VOO over IVV | 2010-09-09 → | +0.86 | +0.15 | +1.62 | +1.03 (+0.88) | 2014: **−56.5 bp** |
| QQQM over QQQ | 2020-10-13 → | +7.19 | **+5.27** | +8.35 | +7.88 (+11.10) | 2023: +10.1 bp |

Two funds that charge the *same* fee cannot have a real −56 bp year against each other. Those
outliers are adjustment artefacts in the public total-return series — a distribution timed
into the wrong session — and they are **an order of magnitude larger than the 5–6 bp gap
being measured**. Drop the best and worst year and VOO-over-SPY lands on +5.48 bp/yr at
*t* = +4.65, i.e. on its prospectus gap. The full-sample insignificance is a **measurement**
failure of the older tape, not evidence that the fee gap is absent — but note that this is an
argument, not a result: **on the full histories the S&P pairs do not clear |*t*| = 2.**

The power arithmetic makes the same point without any trimming. At the observed annual
dispersion, a one-sample *t* of 2 on the full IVV/SPY history would need **165 years** of
tape (25 available); on the placebo pair, **2,534 years**. On the common window, where the
dispersion collapses to 3–4 bp, five years are enough.

**Era cut (split 2020-01-01), full histories:**

| Pair | Early | Late |
|---|--:|--:|
| IVV over SPY | +1.14 (*t* +0.30) | **+5.78** (*t* +2.92) |
| VOO over SPY | +0.73 (*t* +0.12) | **+6.60** (*t* +3.40) |
| VOO over IVV (placebo) | +1.66 (*t* +0.18) | +0.82 (*t* +0.75) |

The "late" rows are arithmetically the common-window rows: chaining anchors on the last
observation of 2020 either way, so both slices reduce to the same five annual differences.
The era cut is therefore *not* independent evidence for the S&P pairs — it is the same five
numbers seen twice, and it is reported here only to show where the older tape stops
cooperating. QQQ/QQQM, split 2023-01-01, is a genuine cut of its own sample: **+5.52 bp/yr**
early (*t* +1.68, two complete years) and **+7.42 bp/yr** late (*t* +7.93, three complete
years) — same sign, same size, both halves. (Its bootstrap CI is `nan` in both halves: fewer
than three complete years, so the interval is refused rather than faked.)

## The break-even curve — a swept spread ASSUMPTION, common window

A daily-close tape carries no quotes, so the extra round-trip spread you pay to use the cheap
wrapper is swept end to end. Break-even = Δspread / TD × 252 trading days.

| Δ round-trip spread | IVV/SPY | VOO/SPY | QQQM/QQQ | VOO/IVV (placebo) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.5 bp | 22 d | 19 d | 18 d | 153 d |
| 1 bp | 44 d | 38 d | 35 d | 307 d |
| 2 bp | 87 d | 76 d | 70 d | 613 d |
| 5 bp | 218 d | 191 d | 175 d | 1,533 d |

**At the pessimistic end of the honest (Student-*t*) interval, the 1 bp break-even stretches
to 898 d for IVV/SPY, 208 d for VOO/SPY and 74 d for QQQM/QQQ — and to *never* for the
placebo pair.** An earlier draft of this document quoted 71/73/53 d here; those came from the
too-narrow bootstrap interval and were wrong. The point estimate still repays a punitive 5 bp
differential inside nine months, but the tape cannot promise the *size* of the saving to
better than a factor of three.

## The empirical race — every overlapping window, one execution lag, 1 bp extra round trip

Mean edge in bp per window (win rate, HAC *t* with lags = the holding period):

| Hold | IVV over SPY | VOO over SPY | QQQM over QQQ | VOO over IVV (placebo) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21 d | −0.46 (43%, −3.25) | −0.40 (43%, −3.23) | −0.51 (44%, −3.05) | −0.94 (33%, −10.54) |
| 63 d | **+0.72** (62%, +2.34) | **+0.82** (63%, +2.76) | **+0.73** (61%, +2.68) | −0.91 (35%, −6.32) |
| 126 d | +2.64 (78%, +3.84) | +2.73 (79%, +4.15) | +2.65 (79%, +5.19) | −0.91 (37%, −4.37) |
| 252 d | +6.76 (86%, +4.07) | +6.86 (87%, +4.12) | +7.47 (92%, +6.11) | −0.90 (37%, −3.55) |
| 504 d | +16.65 (99%, +4.31) | +16.94 (99%, +4.35) | +19.61 (99%, +6.65) | −0.71 (42%, −4.12) |
| 756 d | +30.33 (100%, +7.33) | +30.66 (100%, +7.70) | +36.81 (99%, +10.43) | −0.67 (40%, −3.48) |
| 1008 d | +39.60 (100%, +35.83) | +40.78 (100%, +36.41) | +48.91 (99%, +57.30) | **+0.18** (51%, +0.35) |

This is the second estimator that leaves the placebo quiet, and it is the one that uses every
window rather than only year-end prints. The cheap wrapper turns positive between 42 and 63
days and clears |*t*| = 2 at 63 days on all three fee-gap pairs. The placebo pair is still
**negative at three years** (−0.67 bp, *t* = −3.48) and only marginally positive at four
(+0.18 bp, *t* = +0.35). *(A previous draft said the placebo "never repays over four years";
it is negative through three and turns marginally positive at four.)*

**Read only the short rows as inference.** Newey-West needs a small bandwidth relative to the
sample: at 63 days over ~1,370 windows the ratio is 0.05 and the *t* means what it says; at
1008 days over 425 windows it is 2.4, those windows contain barely one independent draw, and
*t* = +35.8 is a bandwidth artefact, not evidence. The same applies to the win rates —
overlapping windows are not independent trials. The 63-day row is the significance claim; the
rest is descriptive.

## Where it stops being bankable — the long/short harvest (borrow SWEPT)

Long the cheap wrapper, short the liquid one, daily-rebalanced, 1 bp one-way on all four
legs. This is the only construction with a short leg, so it is the only one that pays borrow —
an ASSUMPTION, swept, because no borrow curve is on the tape. Common window:

| Pair | Gross | Tracking noise | Net @ 5 bp | Net @ 10 bp | Net @ 25 bp |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| IVV / SPY | +0.95 bp/yr | 71 bp/yr | −4.76 | −9.76 | −24.76 |
| VOO / SPY | +4.53 bp/yr | 77 bp/yr | −1.18 | −6.18 | −21.18 |
| QQQM / QQQ | +1.93 bp/yr | 90 bp/yr | −3.77 | −8.77 | −23.77 |
| **VOO / IVV — the placebo** | **+3.58 bp/yr** | 52 bp/yr | −2.12 | −7.12 | −22.12 |

**The placebo row is the verdict on this construction.** A pair with *no* fee gap harvests
+3.58 bp/yr gross — more than IVV/SPY (+0.95) and more than QQQM/QQQ (+1.93). Daily
rebalancing of a mean-reverting print spread does not capture a fee; it captures noise, and it
gives back most of the buy-and-hold gap (+1.9 bp/yr traded against +7.2 bp/yr held on
QQQ/QQQM). Add a few basis points inside 50–90 bp/yr of tracking noise — a Sharpe near 0.02 —
and **any borrow above ~5 bp/yr buries it**. The fee gap is a wrapper-*selection* saving,
never a trade.

## The Sharpe race, for completeness — and it is the wrong instrument

Excess-of-cash (BIL) annualised Sharpe, common window, **both legs excess of the same cash
series** so the cash leg cancels in the difference:

| Pair | Liquid | Cheap | Difference | HAC *t* on the return difference |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| IVV vs SPY | +0.7802 | +0.7878 | +0.0077 | +0.13 |
| VOO vs SPY | +0.7802 | +0.7932 | +0.0130 | +0.59 |
| VOO vs IVV (placebo) | +0.7878 | +0.7932 | +0.0054 | +0.59 |
| QQQM vs QQQ | +0.7233 | +0.7289 | +0.0056 | +0.11 |

A 6 bp/yr fee gap inside an arm with 17–22% annualised volatility moves Sharpe in the third
decimal, and the placebo's Sharpe difference (+0.0054) is the same size as the real pairs'.
Racing wrappers on Sharpe would have found nothing here, and would have been wrong to.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof — never supports the stamp)

| Planted gap | Recovered | *t* | 95% CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bp/yr (null) | −0.04 | −0.02 | [−3.17, +2.98] |
| 3 bp/yr | +3.41 | +1.19 | — |
| 6 bp/yr | +6.31 | +3.75 | [+3.04, +9.19] |
| 12 bp/yr | +13.63 | +6.62 | — |

The estimator sits on the 45-degree line rather than merely printing something non-zero, and
across eight independent null seeds the mean *t* is −0.04 (sd 0.34) with **0/8** reaching
|*t*| = 2. It does not manufacture tracking differences. Note what this does *not* prove: the
synthetic tape has no mis-timed distributions, so it cannot vouch for the estimator against
the one defect that actually dominates the real series.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Real.** On the common window the cheap wrapper's realised advantage is
  **+5.78 / +6.60 / +7.19 bp/yr** for IVV, VOO and QQQM over their pricier twins, at *t* =
  **+2.92 / +3.40 / +5.27** across five complete years, **positive in 5/5 years on each pair**
  (sign-test *p* = 0.031 each), with Student-*t* intervals clear of zero and magnitudes within
  ~2 bp of the published fee gaps; the same-fee **placebo prints +0.82 bp/yr (*t* = +0.75,
  3/5 years)** and stays negative for three years in the overlapping race. Named caveats, all
  of them load-bearing: (1) the measured quantity is **fee gap + unit-investment-trust cash
  drag**, unseparated, because the expensive leg is a UIT in every pair that shows a gap;
  (2) the result is **estimator-conditional** — the raw cumulative drift over the same window
  gives IVV/SPY +3.38 against the placebo's +4.69, and only the complete-calendar-year rule
  (fixed ex ante, justified by a +23.6 bp six-month stub artefact on a zero-gap pair) separates
  them; (3) the **full pre-2020 histories fail |*t*| = 2** because the public series carries
  single-year artefacts of −41 to −57 bp; (4) all four pairs rest on the *same* five years, so
  the three fee-gap results are not four independent samples; (5) the funds are survivors.
- **Tradability — Investable.** Not because the tape pins the number down — it does not — but
  because the act is a **purchase decision with no forecast, no timing, no turnover and no
  capacity limit** (these are the largest ETFs in existence, and the fee differential is a
  contractual deduction from NAV that the tape confirms rather than discovers). The break-even
  holding period is **35–44 trading days** at a 1 bp round-trip differential (42–63 days
  measured on overlapping windows with one execution lag), and under nine months at a punitive
  5 bp. What the tape *cannot* promise is the size: at the pessimistic end of the honest
  interval the same 1 bp differential takes **74 days (QQQM/QQQ), 208 (VOO/SPY) and 898
  (IVV/SPY)** to repay. The boundary is equally clear: it is worth **~6 bp/yr**, it never
  justifies churning an existing position, and the long/short version of the same gap is dead
  at any borrow above ~5 bp/yr — where a same-fee placebo pair "harvests" more than two of the
  three real ones.
- **What the study does not claim.** Nothing about intraday spreads (not on this tape),
  nothing about options-market depth or tax-lot effects, nothing that separates the fee from
  the trust form, and nothing about which wrapper will be cheapest next year — fee schedules
  are a competitive variable, and Study 913 asks the persistence question directly.
